values: Il faut + infinitif expresses a general or impersonal necessity; the person concerned is supplied by context.
Il faut que introduces an explicitly stated subject and requires the subjunctive in the dependent clause.
In the affirmative, il me semble que normally takes the indicative; negation or inversion can favor the subjunctive when doubt is emphasized.
all one has to do is
Common spoken formula presenting an action as the simple or obvious solution; it can sound dismissive depending on tone.

patches.entity_key: il ne s'agit pas de + nom/infinitif

values: The impersonal pronoun il does not refer to a person; the phrase rejects the interpretation or objective that follows de.
Impersonal construction identifying the task or issue at hand; il has no concrete referent and the expression remains singular.
Impersonal construction used to identify what is being discussed; il has no concrete referent.
Expresses advice or preference and requires the subjunctive when followed by an explicit subject and que.
With a present-tense clause, this duration construction indicates a situation begun in the past and still continuing.
Musical instruments are introduced by de, with the required contraction: jouer du piano, de la guitare, des cymbales.
Games and sports are introduced by à, with the required contraction: jouer aux cartes, au tennis.
Introduces the endpoint of an action and requires the subjunctive because the endpoint is viewed as pending from the main-clause perspective.

batch_summary: Added mood, register, and construction guidance for impersonal expressions and clarified the prepositions used with musical instruments, games, and sports.
